summary: This bill designates the Department of Veterans Affairs clinic in Riverhead, New York, as the Private First Class Garfield M. Langhorn VA Clinic.

scores.thoughts: The bill is a ceremonial naming designation for an existing VA clinic. It contains no provisions that authorize, appropriate, or alter any government expenditures, so it has no bearing on spending levels.
No provisions in the bill address tax policy, rates, or revenue measures of any kind.
While the bill references a VA clinic (a public healthcare facility), it only changes the facility's name and makes no changes to healthcare delivery, coverage, funding, or public vs. private models.
The bill contains no language related to firearms, regulations, or gun rights.
No provisions address immigration, visas, borders, or related policies.
The bill has no connection to reproductive health policy or abortion access.
The bill honors a deceased Vietnam veteran but does not alter military budgets, force structure, or defense policy.
No environmental, regulatory, or climate-related provisions appear in the bill.
Although the VA provides benefits to veterans, the bill is limited to naming and does not expand, contract, or modify any safety-net programs.
The bill has no provisions concerning schools, funding, or education policy.
No references to drug enforcement, decriminalization, or related matters.
The bill does not address sentencing, policing, or criminal justice reform.
No trade, tariff, or globalization provisions are present.
The bill neither authorizes new spending nor contains any debt-reduction measures.
No language regarding LGBTQ+ protections or related civil rights.
The bill does not address foreign assistance or international aid.
No provisions relate to voting access, election integrity, or electoral procedures.
The bill contains no technology, data, or privacy regulations.
No labor, union, or employment policy provisions are included.
The bill does not engage with religious exemptions or anti-discrimination rules.
